evidence.paraphrase: Valentin explains his method of deliberately following the unreasonable and odd when no clue exists.
evidence.quote: He said that if one had a clue this was the worst way; but if one had no clue at all it was the best, because there was just the chance that any oddity that caught the eye of the pursuer might be the same that had caught the eye of the pursued.

evidence.paraphrase: Description of Valentin's investigative logic of pursuing the unreasonable.
evidence.quote: In such cases, when he could not follow the train of the reasonable, he coldly and carefully followed the train of the unreasonable.

evidence.paraphrase: The inspector reacts skeptically, wondering if the pursued are madmen.
evidence.quote: the inspector said under his breath, "Are we after escaped lunatics?"

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator contrasts Valentin's unremarkable appearance with his hidden identity and power.
evidence.quote: There was nothing about him to indicate the fact that the grey jacket covered a loaded revolver, that the white waistcoat covered a police card, or that the straw hat covered one of the most powerful intellects in Europe.

evidence.paraphrase: Explanation of Flambeau's technique of microphotography to send secret messages.
evidence.quote: It was he who had kept up an unaccountable and close correspondence with a young lady whose whole letter-bag was intercepted, by the extraordinary trick of photographing his messages infinitesimally small upon the slides of a microscope.
